body:
Running the full SPA e2e suite against cwn-local on 2026-08-08 gave 318 passed /
14 failed. A/B on the same container with main's SPA rebuilt (no local diff)
gave 13 failed — so the failures are pre-existing, not introduced by the change
under test (#1454 / #1396).

The two failure sets overlap but are NOT identical, which is the flake tell:

  both runs:      a11y duplicates, a11y reader, a11y admin, edit-rating
                  (desktop + mobile), hidden-books, theme desktop,
                  tag-quick-add-typeahead mobile
  diff-run only:  a11y account, browse "open a book detail", browse "open the
                  reader" (mobile), tag-quick-add-typeahead desktop
  main-run only:  a11y edit-book, a11y announcement, a11y book-detail mobile,
                  theme mobile

Two distinct causes are likely mixed in here and should be separated before
either is chased:

1. Genuine pre-existing a11y breakage. The admin/light contrast violations are
   deterministic and reproduce on both runs (e.g. #9aa7b2 on #ffffff = 2.45:1,
   and #23292f on #1b2530 = 1.05:1 on the settings labels). Those look like a
   real light-theme token defect, not flake.
2. Order-dependent state pollution. The specs mutate library data and the local
   library carries residue from prior runs — a tag literally named
   "... e2e-1785947780250" is sitting in the fixture. Specs that hide books,
   set ratings, and add tags are the ones that move between runs.

Why this matters beyond tidiness: a suite that is red by default cannot gate
anything. Every future change has to run this same A/B to learn whether its own
failures are real, which is a per-change cost and an obvious place for a real
regression to hide in the noise.

Not filed as a tracker issue: no user reported it, per the findings-ledger rule.
title: Local SPA e2e suite is red and flaky on main (13-14 failures, shifting set)
